result.summary:
Independently re-verified REQ-035 (organizer approve/reject surface, GitHub issue #67) end to end; ready to merge.

COMMANDS I RAN MYSELF (not copied from TEST-RUNNER):
- `npm run lint -w apps/bot`: PASS, zero errors.
- `npm run build -w apps/bot` (tsc -p tsconfig.json): PASS, zero errors.
- `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from the REPO ROOT (matching TEST-RUNNER's own scope, not apps/bot's own vitest config which pulls in unrelated suites and reports 716): run TWICE by me, both times 'Test Files 39 passed (39)' / 'Tests 358 passed (358)' -- exact match to TEST-RUNNER's post-rework report, zero variance across my two runs.
- `apps/bot/src/domain/registrationApproval.db.test.ts` (the AC5 concurrency file) run in ISOLATION TWICE MORE by me, independently, from repo root: 7/7 passed both times, including both AC5 cases (20x2 last-seat race, 5x10-fan-in dedicated-pool race with pool.totalCount>1 evidence). This adds my own 2 clean runs on top of the 5 prior clean runs recorded across TEST-RUNNER's two full-suite runs and three isolated reruns -- 7 total clean executions of this file now on record, zero flakiness observed by anyone.
- `apps/bot/src/handlers/organizerRequests.db.test.ts` also spot-run in isolation by me: 8/8 passed (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC6 x2, AC7, AC9 x2).

AC-BY-AC INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION (read the real code/tests myself, not the design doc's claims):
- AC1: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts:1809-1827 -- approveRequest's writing branch calls generateQrToken() (the pre-existing function at line 91, confirmed by reading the call site directly -- no second generator exists anywhere in the diff), UPDATEs admission='admitted' and qrToken in one statement. organizerRequests.db.test.ts's AC1 case reads the row back and asserts a 64-hex-char qrToken plus a captured notification containing the event title. PASS.
- AC2: registration.ts:1893 sets admission='rejected'; handlers/organizerRequests.ts's sendRejectionNotification (line ~511) always joins the organizer's verbatim reason with catalog.event.deepLinkSeeUpcoming in the same message, unconditionally. AC2's db test captures the actual message and asserts both substrings present. PASS.
- AC3: I ran my own grep directly (`grep -ril wishlist apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts apps/bot/drizzle/*.sql`) -- zero matches, exit 1. PASS.
- AC4: registration.ts:1705-1720 decideApprovalOutcome's first-match-wins table -- row 3 approve when seatsLeft>0, row 4 approve-override only when overrideConfirmed, row 5 needs-override-confirmation otherwise. Read the handler (organizerRequests.ts:462-474): the Cancel callback (req:approve_cancel) makes NO domain call at all -- only replies with a static note -- so 'dismiss leaves admission=requested unchanged' is true by construction, not by a runtime check. AC4's db test independently drives all three states (blocked, dismissed, confirmed) and asserts exactly one audit_log row with action registration.approve_override appears only after confirmation. I spot-read this test's assertions directly (not summarized) -- correct. PASS.
- AC5 (this release's most security-critical property): registration.ts:1747-1829 -- approveRequest locks the registrations row FOR UPDATE first, then locks the events row FOR UPDATE, then re-counts admitted registrations INSIDE the same transaction, then calls the pure decideApprovalOutcome, then conditionally writes. This is the same row-lock-then-recount-then-write shape REQ-020/023/030 already establish (traced myself against registration.ts's other transactional writers, not just trusted from the design doc's claim). I independently re-ran the concurrency test file twice in isolation (see above) plus confirmed it inside two full-suite runs -- 4 of my own executions, all green, on top of 3 prior TEST-RUNNER executions -- 7 total. The two AC5 cases construct a genuine race: Promise.all of two/ten concurrent approveRequest calls (the fan-in case uses a dedicated pool with max:30 and asserts pool.totalCount>1 mid-flight as direct evidence of real concurrent connections, not serialized single-connection calls) against a capacity-1 event, and assert exactly one 'approve' outcome and the rest 'needs-override-confirmation' every time, with a final admitted-row count of exactly 1. PASS -- genuinely re-derived, not accepted on report alone.
- AC6: eventAuthorization.ts:60-78's checkOrganizerForChapter refuses role==='member' unconditionally with {ok:false, reason:'not-organizer'} before ever consulting event_staff -- read this function directly. organizerRequests.db.test.ts's AC6 block has two separate cases: a plain member, and a member who is ALSO added to event_staff via addEventStaff -- both invoke req:approve:<id> directly (constructed callback data, not a rendered button tap) and both assert the registration row is unchanged (admission still 'requested', qrToken still null), zero audit rows added, zero notifications sent, and the exact notAuthorized catalog string returned. I read both test bodies myself; the assertions are real DB re-reads, not just outcome.kind checks. PASS.
- AC7: organizerRequests.ts's approve handler (makeRequestApproveCallbackHandler, lines 380-419) resolves the registration's OWN event and calls requireOrganizerForChapter against THAT event's chapterId, not the caller's stored chapterId -- confirmed by reading the handler body directly. AC7's test constructs chapter A and chapter B, an organizer scoped to A, a request against B's event, invokes approve, and re-reads the row (still 'requested', qrToken null, zero audit delta, zero notifications). PASS.
- AC8: listPendingRequestsForOrganizer's and getPendingRequestForOrganizer's select() clauses (registration.ts:1599-1616, 1645-1663) name only registrationId/userId/firstName/lastName/tgUsername/company/position/isStudent/source/createdAt/admission -- profiles.phone and profiles.email are structurally absent, not filtered post-fetch. The registrationApproval.db.test.ts AC8 case is a real negative control: seeds a profile with BOTH a real phone and email, renders both the list view AND the detail view, serializes each (text + JSON.stringify(keyboard)), asserts neither secret string nor a partial-digit fragment of the phone appears, and includes a positive control (company string IS present) so the negative assertions aren't vacuous. I read this test's fixture and assertions directly. PASS.
- AC9: sendApprovalNotification and sendRejectionNotification (organizerRequests.ts ~479-543) both call sendLedgeredNotification with classification:'transactional' passed explicitly (never defaulted, no '?' on the type per notification.ts). AC9's two db-test cases explicitly set broadcastOptIn:false on the registrant before each action and assert the message still lands, then re-read the user row to confirm the flag was never flipped to make the test pass. PASS.
- AC10: approveRequest and rejectRequest each call writeAuditLog exactly once, inside the same transaction as the UPDATE, only on the writing branches (not-found/not-requested/needs-override-confirmation all return before any write). AC10's db tests (registrationApproval.db.test.ts) correctly account for registerForEvent's own pre-existing unconditional 'registration.request' audit row by asserting a baseline of 1 before the action under test, then asserting exactly +1 after -- this is the exact bug TEST-RUNNER caught and TEST-DESIGNER fixed in the rework iteration (commit 13598de); I independently confirmed the fix is correct by reading registration.ts:242-254's registerForEvent audit write myself and reading the corrected baselines in both test files (both now assert before===1, not before===0). PASS.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE (independently re-run, not trusted from any report): `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.ts` is EMPTY -- REQ-029's overrideAdmitAndCheckIn is untouched. `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts apps/bot/drizzle/` is EMPTY -- no schema/migration change, matching the design's explicit 'no DATA-DESIGNER needed' claim. `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/index.ts` is pure handler-registration wiring (new imports + 7 new bot.command/bot.callbackQuery/bot.on registrations), no logic change. Full diff stat: 23 files changed, 4650 insertions, 0 deletions -- entirely new files/additions, nothing rewritten.

STALENESS CHECK against docs/agents/requirements.yaml and docs/status/requirement_status.yaml: REQ-035's requirements.yaml entry still reads status: pending (not in_progress), and requirement_status.yaml has NO 'started' event for REQ-035 at all -- the last entries are REQ-034's 'done' event. This is a Step 00 bookkeeping gap (ORCH's responsibility per WF-02 Step 00: 'ORCH flips status to in_progress and appends a started event' -- this did not happen for this run, confirmed by re-reading handoffs/WF02-REQ-035/step-00-git-setup.json, which only records branch creation, no status-file edit). This does not block a PASS verdict on the requirement's actual acceptance criteria (all 10 are independently confirmed satisfied by the shipped code), but DOC-UPDATER/ORCH must backfill the missing 'started' event (with an honest historical timestamp note, since the real start time is not recoverable exactly) before or alongside appending the 'done' event, and must correct requirements.yaml's status from pending directly to done (skipping the never-recorded in_progress) -- flagging this explicitly so it is not silently glossed over.

VERDICT: PASS. All 10 acceptance criteria independently re-verified against actual code and real test assertions. Lint/build/full-suite/concurrency-file all re-run by this validator with exact matching counts. Scope discipline clean. Ready to merge, with the one non-blocking bookkeeping gap named above for DOC-UPDATER to close.

Per WF-02_requirement_implementation.md's Step 00: 'On PASS: ORCH flips the requirement(s)' status to in_progress ... and appends a started event'. This did not happen. Non-blocking for this PASS verdict since the actual shipped code/tests independently satisfy all 10 ACs, but DOC-UPDATER should flip requirements.yaml directly pending -> done (there was no real in_progress window recorded) and should consider backfilling or noting the missing 'started' event in its own 'done' event's note so the gap is documented rather than silently smoothed over.
